subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats get a first-class opt-in dynamic per-sender agent mode, or should OpenClaw keep group isolation to session scopes, static bindings, and explicit subagent/thread commands?
rationale: Current source proves the requested group dynamic-agent behavior is missing, but adding it changes product architecture and security boundaries across Feishu routing, persistent sessions, per-agent state, group permissions, and subagent lifecycle.

options.title: Design Opt-In Group Sender Agents
options.body: Add a Feishu plugin-owned opt-in mode for group sender agents with explicit lifecycle, memory, authorization, resource limits, and migration behavior before code changes.

options.title: Defer Behind Session/Threading Work
options.body: Keep this issue open but wait for related session-key, channel threading, and skill-preference decisions to settle before choosing the Feishu group orchestration shape.

options.title: Decline Dynamic Group Agents
options.body: Document `groupSessionScope`, static bindings, ACP thread bindings, and explicit `sessions_spawn` as the supported patterns, leaving per-member agent orchestration to external plugins or deployments.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Group Sender Agents
recommendation.body: Add a Feishu plugin-owned opt-in mode for group sender agents with explicit lifecycle, memory, authorization, resource limits, and migration behavior before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal on current Feishu dynamic routing, account scoping, and recent review history for the affected behavior.
